newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard cuts prices of laptop PCs.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard cuts prices of laptop PCs.

text.p: Computer maker Hewlett-Packard Co said on Monday it has cut prices on its HP OmniBook 5500 notebook PC series by as much as 21 percent to increase its share of the business market sector, effective immediately.

The company said in a statement that the move, which will see U.S. list prices of its HP OmniBook 5500CS 5/100 notebook PC model 810, fall as low as $2,200, is aimed at making its line of laptop computers more attractive to business customers.
"This aggressive price drop marks an important expansion of HP's corporate notebook PC offering," said Andrew Zaremba, product marketing manager at Hewlett-Packard.
"We think that the new, wider range of price points, coupled with the traditional HP strengths of quality and reliability, makes HP the most attractive choice for the corporate buyer," he added.
Shares of Hewlett-Packard were 1-1/8 higher at 48-1/2 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
